strings.d1.s0.name: Grand-Place
strings.d1.s0.tips: UNESCO-listed square with guildhalls and the Town Hall, empty before 10:00. Manneken Pis is 2 streets away. In even-numbered years the Flower Carpet appears in August.
strings.d1.s1.name: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
strings.d1.s1.tips: Glass-roofed arcade from 1847. Home to Neuhaus's first shop and Pierre Marcolini.
strings.d1.s2.name: Maison Dandoy Grand-Place
strings.d1.s2.tips: Speculoos and Brussels waffles (rectangular, light) since 1829. Compare with the Liège waffle (dense, sugary).
strings.d1.s3.name: Fritland
strings.d1.s3.tips: A friterie beside the square. Try double-fried chips and a mitraillette sandwich, part of UNESCO-recognised culture.
strings.d1.s4.name: Delirium Café
strings.d1.s4.tips: Guinness record holder with 2,000+ beers. Find it on Impasse de la Fidélité, opposite Jeanneke Pis.
strings.d1.b0.name: Chez Léon
strings.d1.b0.tips: Moules-frites (mussels and chips) since 1893, on Rue des Bouchers.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museum of the City of Brussels Maison du Roi
strings.d1.b1.tips: The city museum in the King's House on the square. Includes Manneken Pis costumes.
strings.d2.s0.name: Magritte Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: 200+ surrealist works (bowler hat, apple). Combined ticket with the Royal Museums is 15, closed Monday.
strings.d2.s1.name: Place du Grand Sablon
strings.d2.s1.tips: Antique dealers and chocolatiers (Wittamer, Marcolini). Antiques market at weekends.
strings.d2.s2.name: Le Pain Quotidien Sablon
strings.d2.s2.tips: The chain's first branch. Tartines and soup.
strings.d2.s3.name: Place du Jeu de Balle Flea Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: Daily flea market in the Marolles (best in the morning), Brueghel's old neighbourhood.
strings.d2.s4.name: Musical Instruments Museum MIM
strings.d2.s4.tips: Housed in the Art Nouveau Old England building. Instruments with headphones, and a rooftop café with views.
strings.d2.b0.name: Wittamer Sablon
strings.d2.b1.name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
strings.d2.b1.tips: Bruegel and Rubens. An alternative to MIM (combined ticket with Magritte).
strings.d3.s0.name: Markt Bruges
strings.d3.s0.tips: 1 hour by train (Brussels-Midi, about 15 EUR). Belfry square and guildhalls.
strings.d3.s1.name: Belfry of Bruges
strings.d3.s1.tips: 366 steps to the bell chamber and a panorama of the canal city. Timed tickets.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bruges Canal Boat Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: 30-minute boat ride. Passes Rozenhoedkaai (the most photographed corner), 5 landing stages.
strings.d3.s3.name: De Halve Maan Brewery
strings.d3.s3.tips: Home of Brugse Zot beer. 45-minute tour plus a beer, rooftop views, good for lunch.
strings.d3.s4.name: Begijnhof Bruges
strings.d3.s4.tips: Beguine courtyard from 1245, peaceful. Minnewater, the Lake of Love, is nearby.
strings.d3.b0.name: Frituur Bruges Markt
strings.d3.b0.tips: Two chip huts beneath the Belfry.
strings.d3.b1.name: Groeningemuseum
strings.d3.b1.tips: Flemish Primitives (van Eyck). Instead of the Begijnhof.
strings.d4.s0.name: Atomium
strings.d4.s0.tips: The 102 m steel crystal from Expo 1958. Spheres and views, book online (combined Design Museum ticket).
strings.d4.s1.name: Mini-Europe
strings.d4.s1.tips: 350 miniatures of Europe at the foot of the Atomium, good with children.
strings.d4.s2.name: Atomium Restaurant
strings.d4.s2.tips: Restaurant with views in the top sphere. Alternatively, use the café outside.
strings.d4.s3.name: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken
strings.d4.s3.tips: Closed (open in spring only). See Laeken Park and the Chinese Pavilion from outside, then move on to Cinquantenaire.
strings.d4.s4.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
strings.d4.s4.tips: Triumphal arch and museums, in the EU quarter.
strings.d4.b0.name: Frit Flagey
strings.d4.b0.tips: The city's best friterie (Place Flagey). Go by tram.
strings.d4.b1.name: Autoworld Cinquantenaire
strings.d4.b1.tips: 300 classic cars. Instead of the park.
strings.d5.s0.name: Gravensteen
strings.d5.s0.tips: 35 minutes by train. The counts' castle, with a funny audio guide and city views from the ramparts.
strings.d5.s1.name: Graslei & Korenlei
strings.d5.s1.tips: Canal-side guildhalls. The best view in Ghent, from St Michael's Bridge.
strings.d5.s2.name: Saint Bavo's Cathedral Ghent Altarpiece
strings.d5.s2.tips: Van Eyck's Adoration of the Mystic Lamb panels (AR tour). Opposite the Belfry.
strings.d5.s3.name: Patershol
strings.d5.s3.tips: Medieval quarter with restaurants. Try Gentse waterzooi (chicken stew soup).
strings.d5.s4.name: Ghent Canal Boat Tour
strings.d5.s4.tips: 40 minutes, departing from Graslei. Then take the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Belfry of Ghent
strings.d5.b0.tips: UNESCO-listed bell tower. Instead of the cathedral.
strings.d5.b1.name: Frituur Filip Gent
strings.d6.theme: Ixelles, Art Nouveau and the EU
strings.d6.s0.name: Horta Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: Home of Victor Horta, the inventor of Art Nouveau, in Saint-Gilles. Timed tickets, closed Monday.
strings.d6.s1.name: Avenue Louise Art Nouveau Walk
strings.d6.s1.tips: Hôtel Tassel and Solvay facades in Ixelles.
strings.d6.s2.name: Place Flagey & Ixelles Ponds
strings.d6.s2.tips: Square and lakeside. Market at weekends.
strings.d6.s3.name: Belga Café Flagey
strings.d6.s3.tips: Café on Place Flagey. Croque and beer, opposite Frit Flagey.
strings.d6.s4.name: European Parliament Parlamentarium
strings.d6.s4.tips: Free interactive EU museum. Hemicycle tour with your passport.
strings.d6.b0.name: Moeder Lambic Fontainas
strings.d6.b0.tips: Bar for lambic and gueuze beers. A local alternative to Delirium.
strings.d6.b1.name: Museum of Natural Sciences
strings.d6.b1.tips: Europe's largest dinosaur hall. Instead of the Parlamentarium.
strings.d7.s0.name: Choco-Story Brussels
strings.d7.s0.tips: Chocolate museum with demonstrations, next to the Grand-Place.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pierre Marcolini Grand Sablon
strings.d7.s1.tips: One of Belgium's best chocolatiers. Buy a gift box.
strings.d7.s2.name: Noordzee Mer du Nord
strings.d7.s2.tips: Stand-up fish bar on Sainte-Catherine. Shrimp croquettes and white wine for a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Gare Centrale
strings.d7.s3.tips: Train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes (Midi/Central). Bus to Charleroi takes 1 hour. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Le Pain Quotidien Sainte-Catherine
strings.d7.b1.name: Comics Art Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: Tintin and the Smurfs in a Horta building. Instead of the chocolate stops.
strings.note0: A STIB day pass is 8 EUR, and the city centre is walkable. Take the train to Bruges and Ghent (50% off weekend tickets). The train to Zaventem takes 20 minutes.
strings.note1: Summer is 20-25°C, and rain is always possible. Look out for the Ommegang (July) and the August Flower Carpet in even-numbered years. Bruges is very crowded and the Laeken greenhouses are closed.
strings.note2: Waffles cost 3-7 EUR (Brussels = rectangular and light, Liège = dense and sugary), frites 4-6, moules-frites 25, beer 4-6. Tip by rounding up.
strings.note3: In Belgium, French is spoken in Brussels and Flemish in Bruges and Ghent. English is also widely spoken. Avoid the restaurants on Rue des Bouchers (tourist traps), with Chez Léon the exception.
strings.note4: Museums are closed on Mondays. Book Atomium and Belfry online. On the first Wednesday of the month, many museums are free in the afternoon.
strings.note5: Chocolate: Neuhaus, Marcolini, Wittamer, Mary. Leonidas is cheap and good.
